briefdescription.para: The length of the critical path through a trace is the maximum of two path lengths:

listitem.para: The maximum height+depth over all instructions in the trace center block.
The longest cross-block dependency chain. For small blocks, it is possible that the critical path through the trace doesn't include any instructions in the block.

detaileddescription.para: This function computes the second number from the live-in list of the center block.

briefdescription.para: Compute instruction depths for all instructions above or in MBB in its trace.

detaileddescription.para: This assumes that the trace through MBB has already been computed.

briefdescription.para: Compute instruction heights in the trace through MBB.

detaileddescription.para: This updates MBB and the blocks below it in the trace. It is assumed that the trace has already been computed.

memberdef.argsstring: (const MachineInstr *DefMI, unsigned DefOp, ArrayRef< const MachineBasicBlock * > Trace)
memberdef.name: addLiveIns

briefdescription.para: Assuming that the virtual register defined by DefMI:DefOp was used by Trace.back(), add it to the live-in lists of all the blocks in Trace.

detaileddescription.para: Stop when reaching the block that contains DefMI.

briefdescription.para: Get an array of processor resource depths for MBB.

detaileddescription.para: Indexed by processor resource kind, this array contains the scaled processor resources consumed by all blocks preceding MBB in its trace. It does not include instructions in MBB.

briefdescription.para: Get an array of processor resource heights for MBB.

detaileddescription.para: Indexed by processor resource kind, this array contains the scaled processor resources consumed by this block and all blocks following it in its trace.

briefdescription.para: Get the trace that passes through MBB.

detaileddescription.para: The trace is computed on demand.

briefdescription.para: Updates the depth of an machine instruction, given RegUnits.
Updates the depth of the instructions from Start to End.
A trace ensemble is a collection of traces selected using the same strategy, for example 'minimum resource height'.

detaileddescription.para: There is one trace for every block in the function.
